jobs.description: At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.The PositionWe are looking for a Technical Specialist (m/f/d) for the Regional Customer Support Center (RCSC), based in Mannheim (Germany)*. On a daily basis, we support numerous customers from seven countries and provide remote, telephone and email support for inquiries, technical questions and complaints regarding our Roche analytical systems. That’s what moves us: Safe and easy routines for our customers means more patients we can help. We are proud of who we are, what we do and how we do it, with a clear goal in mind: Doing now what patients need next.The OpportunityOur international Regional Customer Support Center (RCSC) is responsible for technical and application customer service for Roche analytical systems in in-vitro laboratory diagnostics. As an Technical Specialist (m/w/d), you will be the direct contact for inquiries from our customers in diagnostic laboratories and hospitals in the RCSC countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Greece and Turkey). Your main tasks are:* You will support our customers in hospitals and diagnostic laboratories in the Netherlands and Belgium as well as colleagues in the field by telephone, digitally and via remote connection and support them from the acceptance of technical product problems to the derivation of suitable measures for problem solving.* You identify the causes of product problems, work out solutions and initiate appropriate measures.* You carefully document your activities in the supporting customer relationship management (CRM) system.* You prepare product information and support the transfer of information to the customer and the exchange of knowledge within the organization.* *We are flexible as to where you work. Your place of work can be Mannheim (Germany) or Almere (The Netherlands). In any case, you will actively seek the exchange and cooperation with your colleagues at the RCSC in Mannheim* Occasionally, you conduct customer training sessions in the local language.* Occasionally, you support field service colleagues during on-site service visits to the customer lab.Who you are* You are fluent in Dutch/Flemish, and English. Ideally, you also speak German or another language such as Turkish or Greek.* You have successfully completed your engineering studies (e.g. medical technology, electrical engineering, mechatronics) or degree. Alternatively, you have trained as a technician or computer scientist plus professional experience.* Ideally, you have several years of experience in the medical-technical field, through technical customer support (field service or hotline) or in a laboratory function.* You have in-depth knowledge of technology (mechanics, electrical engineering). You are familiar with IT network structures, communication protocols and IT interfaces and have experience in the area of server operating systems.* You are quick on the uptake and can solve complex problems in a structured manner using your analytical skills.* You are open minded and have intercultural experience.* You show a high degree of communicative and social competence in personal and virtual cooperation. Working in a team is your strength.* Customer satisfaction is your strongest motivation.So far, so good? It gets even better. We offer you a wide range of top benefits  at our locations. Only with you can we improve the lives of patients. Your contribution makes Roche unique. That's why we offer exceptional benefits that support you in shaping your life, your finances, and your health the way you want. Find out more here: https://go.roche.com/Kandidaten-Benefits-DECV only - Simply upload your CV and apply!Your contact to us! With people. For people.Do you need further support?Please have a look at our FAQs, you will find them via https://careers.roche.com/global/en/faq.Who we areA healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.Let’s build a healthier future, together.Roche is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

jobs.occupation: Researcher (m/f/d) in Deep-Sea Biodiversity and Taxonomy (Meeresbiologe/-biologin)
jobs.description: Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN) , headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position in the Department of Marine Zoologyat the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum Frankfurt, starting as soon as 06 January 2027:** Researcher (m/f/d) in Deep-Sea Biodiversity and Taxonomy****(Part-Time: 50%)**Employment scope: 50%Part-TimeType of contract: Limited to 1 year (06 January 2027to 10 February 2028)Remuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The city of Frankfurt, where the Senckenberg Society was originally founded, hosts the organization’s central administrative services along with two research institutes housing extensive scientific collections and one of Senckenberg’s most renowned institutions, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum Frankfurt. Senckenberg is as much a part of the city’s identity as its skyline and its traditional apple wine.Funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG), the HADALquake project investigates how earthquake-induced submarine landslides affect life and elemental cycles in the deepest parts of the ocean. The project focuses on comparing conditions before and after recent earthquakes in the Kermadec and Tonga trench systems in the South Pacific.Your tasks- The scientist is primarily responsible for processing of the benthic animal groups:- Assistance in sorting the benthic material- Quantitative extraction and determination of the macrofauna with special consideration of an abundant, selected taxon, such as the Isopoda or another peracarid taxon.- Biodiversity analysis and analysis of biogeography of the Isopoda- Biogeographical comparison of selected taxon with previous data from the South Pacific- Preparation of individuals for genetic analysis (barcoding gene fragments and other gene fragments to support taxonomic questions and phylogenetic analysesYour profile- A completed university degree (Master’s or equivalent) in biology, marine biology or a related discipline.- Research experience in the taxonomy, biodiversity and biogeography of deep-sea benthic invertebrates, particularly isopod crustaceans.- Practical experience in scientific research cruises, biological sample processing and species identification.- Experience in biodiversity data management and statistical analyses using R.- Good written and spoken English.- Willingness and availability to participate in the research expedition: 06 January 2027, departure in Suva, Fidschi to 10 February 2028, arriving in Wellington, New Zealand.Desirable skills- Knowledge of deep-sea sampling. Identification of deep-sea Isopoda, Amphipoda and/or another peracarid taxon (Crustacea, Malacostraca).We offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Women are particularly encouraged to apply, as they are underrepresented in the field of this position; in the case of equal qualifications and suitability they will be given preference. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV, certificates of academic achievements, list of publications as well as letter(s) of recommendation, if available) electronically as a single PDF by 08.11.2026.Please submit your application via our online application system. If you are viewing this vacancy on an external job platform, please visit our careers page and apply via the corresponding "Apply" button. Applications submitted by email cannot be considered.ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt am MainFor specific questions about this role, please contact Prof. Dr. Angelika Brandt atangelika.brandt@senckenberg.de

You don't just oversee compliance – you actively get your hands dirty solving the technical problems that stand between an idea and a certified aircraft.You lead our Engineering, Development, and Certification functions, coordinate external Compliance Verification Engineers, and act as the technical interface to the independent Head of Airworthiness, ensuring robust oversight, clear accountability, and the highest standards of regulatory compliance. and Design Assurance Responsibilities- Establish, maintain, and continuously improve the documented Design Assurance System — hands-on, not just on paper.- Ensure that all design work is undertaken in accordance with the Design Assurance System, BCAR A8-21, and other applicable airworthiness regulations.- Ensure that all design activities remain within the scope of the company's approved design privileges.- Ensure that for all design work, compliance with the applicable type certification basis or equivalent is properly demonstrated and verified.- Ensure that flight testing is carried out in accordance with regulatory requirements.- Sign Declarations of Compliance after satisfactory verification of compliance with applicable airworthiness requirements.- Confirm that all design procedures specified in the Design Organisation Exposition have been followed by signing a Declaration of Compliance for each type approval, type certification, design change, or repair design.Organisational and Management Responsibilities- Lead and manage the Engineering, Development, and Certification functions of the Design Organisation, staying close to the technical detail rather than managing from a distance.- Manage and coordinate external Compliance Verification Engineers.- Provide technical oversight and interface to the independent Head of Airworthiness function.- Ensure qualification, competency, and training of engineering and certification personnel.- Coordinate and manage design, development, certification, and flight test programmes with internal and external stakeholders.- Provide strong project management across design, development, certification, and flight test programmes — planning, scheduling, and managing resources with internal and external stakeholders to keep programmes on time and on budget.- Provide technical authority for design decisions, certification strategies, and design changes, personally stepping in when problems get stuck between departments.- Ensure complete, controlled, and traceable design documentation for certification, production, continued airworthiness, and future investigations.- Provide technical support to production, quality, customer support, and incident investigations where required.- Actively identify inefficiencies and gaps in existing processes and drive their resolution with an entrepreneurial, get-it-done mindset.Required Qualifications- Degree in Aerospace, Mechanical, or Electrical Engineering, or a comparable technical qualification.- Extensive professional experience in a regulated industrial environment; experience gained within a German company as well as senior-level experience from the automotive industry are highly desirable.- Proven track record in leading engineering teams, driving technical decisions, and taking full accountability for results, timelines, and compliance.- Strong and practical expertise in complex systems engineering, including electrical and avionics integration.- Solid experience with regulatory frameworks and compliance environments (e.g. DULV BUT, BCAR Section T, UK CAA, FAA, CAAC).- A true problem solver: someone energized rather than deterred by open, unresolved technical challenges, who finds pragmatic paths forward instead of waiting for perfect conditions.- Hands-on, execution-focused leadership style with a high level of assertiveness and decision-making authority — someone who rolls up their sleeves rather than delegating every difficult problem.- Ability to challenge existing structures, enforce standards, and drive implementation across interfaces (Engineering, Certification, Production, Quality).- High level of ownership, resilience, and confidence when operating in complex, regulated, and time-critical environments.- An intrapreneurial mindset: you treat the Design Organisation as if it were your own venture, take initiative beyond the formal job description, and are comfortable building and improving processes rather than just following them.- English, German & Chinese: mandatory (written and spoken).Benefits- Dynamic working environment with the global leader in gyroplane manufacturing.- Comprehensive onboarding and continuous training opportunities.- Supportive and international team culture.- Flexible working hours (flexitime) to support work–life balance.- Corporate fitness programme (Hansefit).- Employer contributions to the pension scheme.- Employee discounts via our corporate benefits platform.- Regular company events that strengthen team spirit.- Free daily lunch at our headquarter.- Overtime compensation and additional paid leave for special occasions.- Unique aviation experience – including a gyrocopter sightseeing flight.Are you ready for an exciting career in aviation? Then join AutoGyro GmbH.We are the world market leader in the development, production and sale of gyrocopters and work with partners in more than 40 countries. Our headquarters and production facility are located at Hildesheim Airport. With state-of-the-art technologies, a high degree of vertical integration and a clear vision for sustainable aviation, we are actively shaping the future.Since our foundation in 1999, we have grown steadily and now employ an international team of nearly 100 qualified specialists and engineers. Through our global sales network, we are consistently pursuing our goal: to bring the thrill of flying, maximum safety and the versatile applications of the Gyro to people all over the world.

PhD position or Postdoctoral researcher (m/f/d): Effects of global livestock management on wildlife movementSenckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre (SBiK-F), starting as of 01 January2027:PhD position or Postdoctoral researcher (m/f/d):Effects of global livestock management on wildlife movementitel (m/f/d)(Part-Time)Location: Frankfurt am MainEmployment scope: PhD position (65%) / PostDoc (up to 60%)Type of contract: Temporary, limited to 4 years, until 31.12.20230Remuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E 13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The mission of the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre is to study the complex interactions between biodiversity, climate and society.As part of the Centre, the group “Global Land Systems and Biodiversity” takes a system perspective on how production, trade and consumption of food and other biomass products affect ecosystems and people.The VEBITA project, conducted jointly by SGN, the Marburg University and the Institute for Social-Ecological Research (ISOE) brings together researchers and practice partners to work towards utilizing animal movement data for early-warning systems for nature conservation. By analyzing GPS and sensor data from animals with statistical and AI-based methods, VEBITA aims to detect how animal behaviors change in response to land use, climate change, habitat loss, infrastructure development, and other environmental pressures.The adverstised position focuses on the effects of livestock management on wildlife movements contributes a use-case for state-of-the art animal movement data. Currently, livestock keeping has the largest spatial footprint of all land uses and the global biomass of mammalian livestock exceeds that of all remaining wild mammals by an order of magnitude. How and where livestock are kept greatly impacts the movements of the remaining wild mammals.In this context, we seek to develop a refined biodiversity footprint approach that captures how different livestock management strategies impact movement of wild mammals and how management can be adapted to achieve more sustainable outcomes. This subproject is part of VEBITA’s transdisciplinary focus, and the design of the novel footprint approach will consider perspectives of different relevant societal stakeholder groups such as livestock farmers, conservationists, and regulators. Results and insights of this work will also feed back to international science-policy debates on how conservation and human activities can be aligned in the future.Your tasks- Advance existing biodiversity footprint approaches in the context of livestock production and wildlife movement- Classify global livestock management systems- Analyze global patterns of how livestock keeping influences movements of wild mammals- Actively engage in exchange and cooperation within VEBITA’s inter- and transdisciplinary project team- Participate in project meetings and contribute to project reporting- Publish results in international journals in cooperation with the project teamYour profile- MSc degree (or equivalent) for application for a PhD position or PhD degree for application as postdoctoral researcher in a relevant field, e.g., sustainability science, physical geography, ecology or another relevant field- Programming skills (R, Python or similar), familiarity in working with heterogenous datasets and their analysis- Excellent English language skills- Interest in working in an inter- and transdisciplinary project- Interest in applied science at the science-policy interfaceDesirable skills- Experience with stakeholder interactionsWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application as a single PDF by 19 November 2026, stating the reference number Ref. #11-26021, including:- cover letter describing your motivation to apply for this position- detailed CV- contact details of two potential references- all academic credentials and certificatesPlease submit your application via our online application system. Senckenberg – Leibniz Institution for Biodiversity and Earth System Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at its Department of River Ecology and Conservation in Gelnhausen, starting as soon as possible2 Postdoctoral Researchers (ecologists) (m/f/d)(full-time / part-time)Location: GelnhausenEmployment scope: full-time / part-time options are availableType of contract: limited two years / an extension is be possibleRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) E 13Senckenberg is one of the world’s leading research institutions in the field of Biodiversity and Earth System Research, with eight research institutes and three natural history museums across Germany and scientists from over 40 nations. Our headquarter is located in the thriving commercial metropolis of Frankfurt in the heart of Germany, which also hosts one of our most famous facilities, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum. The location of the available position is in a Senckenberg institute about 40 kilometers east of Frankfurt in Gelnhausen, a historic town accessible via public transport (rail and bus).We are looking for enthusiastic ecologists with a background in broad-scale biodiversity change, community ecology, macroecology, metacommunities, and/or analysis of ecological time series.The two positions are embedded in one or more of the following projects:1. Synthesis Center on Freshwater Biodiversity Change in Europe The Synthesis Center brings together and supports a broad variety of researchers and practitioners investigating a broad variety of fundamental and applied ecological questions, with a particular focus on broad-scale and long-term biodiversity change, community ecology, freshwater ecology, time series analyses, multiple stressor impacts, and conservation (see doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06400-1 for an example). Data for > 30,000 freshwater biodiversity time series across 30 European countries have already been compiled from rivers and lakes, covering invertebrates, fish, macrophytes, diatoms, and benthic algae, in collaboration with a large pan-European network of > 200 researchers. Positions involved in this project are expected to pursue similar questions using the already available data.2. EU Horizon Europe project BEAGLE (started on 1st October 2026)BEAGLE (Biodiversity methods for advanced monitoring at large scales) is an EU-funded project using new technology to enhance biodiversity monitoring across terrestrial, freshwater, and marine environments. Specifically, the project uses sensors, environmental DNA (eDNA) and AI, as well as citizen science to collect large-scale and high-quality biodiversity data across a consortium of 17 partners. Positions involved in this project will focus on several tasks, including European-scale biodiversity data mobilization activities (e.g., tracking down datasets and preparing them for use), and the learning and deployment of field-based methods for data collection (e.g., Malaise traps). Participating researchers will gain experience in broad-scale biodiversity data collection and management, biodiversity monitoring, and participation in European-scale research networks.Your tasks• Contributing scientifically to one or more of the above-described projects (you can indicate a preference in your application if you have one)• Analyzing spatial and temporal biodiversity data, and accompanied environmental data, to elucidate spatial patterns and temporal trends and drivers thereof• Preparing scientific manuscripts• Attending project meetings and preparing project reports• Mentoring graduate students• Giving oral presentations at national and international conferences• Attending virtual and physical project meetingsYour profile• PhD in Ecology or a related field• Solid background in fields related to the above expected tasks for a given project or projects.• Advanced skills in statistical analyses, using R• Skills in project management and report writing are preferred but not essential• Strong publication record for your current career level• Excellent written and oral communication and project presentation skills in EnglishWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity.
